title: Random Number Generation in Javascript: Building a Love Calculator
summary: Explains Math.random() and the scale-floor-shift recipe for producing whole numbers in a range, notes that the numbers are pseudo-random, then has the learner build a love calculator that shows a random 1-100 score.

concepts.heading: Math.random()
points: Math.random() is a built-in function taking no inputs; the parentheses are still required to call it.
It returns a floating-point number from 0 up to but not including 1 (up to about 16 decimal places such as 0.9999...). 0 can occur; 1 never does.
A new value is produced on every call, which makes it useful for games, dice and similar features.
The MDN page for Math.random describes it as pseudo-random with the range [0, 1) and says to scale it to the range you need.

concepts.heading: Scale, floor, shift recipe
points: Multiply by the number of outcomes wanted: n * 6 gives 0 to 5.999...
Wrap in Math.floor() to drop the decimals, giving whole numbers 0 to 5. The result can never be 6.
Add 1 to move the range to 1 through 6. In general: Math.floor(Math.random() * count) + lowest.
Whole numbers are almost always what you want, so floor is nearly always applied.

concepts.heading: Pseudo-random numbers
points: Computers are deterministic, so they produce numbers with algorithms that merely look statistically random; hence pseudo-random.
The lecture points to an extra-reading video in the resources and treats it as optional.

code_examples.caption: Dice roll, 1 to 6
code_examples.code:
var n = Math.random();      // 0 <= n < 1
n = n * 6;                  // 0 <= n < 6
n = Math.floor(n);          // 0..5
n = n + 1;                  // 1..6
console.log(n);

task.name: Love Calculator
task.starting_point: An empty script file (or browser DevTools snippet).
task.goal: Ask for two names, ignore them, and alert a random love score between 1 and 100.
steps: Call prompt() twice, once for each person's name. The answers are not stored because they are never used.
Create a variable loveScore from Math.random().
Multiply it by 100, then wrap in Math.floor() to get whole numbers 0 to 99.
Add 1 so the range becomes 1 to 100.
Show the result with alert("Your love score is " + loveScore + "%").
task.expected_result: Two prompt boxes appear, then an alert with a different whole-number percentage between 1 and 100 on each run.
task.reference_repo_path: Section 15 - Intermediate Javascript/15.01 - Random Number Generation in Javascript - Building a Love Calculator/script.js

pitfalls: Forgetting the parentheses on Math.random, which gives the function rather than a number.
Forgetting + 1, so the range is 0-99 and can never reach 100.
Using Math.round instead of floor, which skews the ends of the range.
Expecting the maximum value to equal the multiplier.

playground.coverage: Covers raw random, the 1-100 love score with alert, dice, coin flip and random list item, plus the formula and pseudo-random note.
gaps_and_ideas: Add the two prompt() calls from the challenge to the task list.
